attachments.origin_landmark: posterior ilium (behind posterior gluteal line), sacrum, coccyx, sacrotuberous ligament
attachments.insertion_landmark: gluteal tuberosity (deep fibers) + iliotibial tract (superficial ~3/4 of fibers)

actions: upper fibers assist abduction, lower fibers assist adduction

functional_compartments.name: Superior segment
functional_compartments.function_note: More vertically-oriented fibers, greater contribution to hip abduction moment; documented independent EMG activation from the inferior segment.
functional_compartments.source: Selkowitz DM, Beneck GJ, Powers CM (2016) J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 46(9):794-799 -- fine-wire EMG confirming superior/inferior gluteus maximus functional segments

functional_compartments.name: Inferior segment
functional_compartments.function_note: More obliquely-oriented fibers, greater hip extension/external rotation moment.
functional_compartments.source: Selkowitz DM, Beneck GJ, Powers CM (2016) J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 46(9):794-799 -- fine-wire EMG confirming superior/inferior gluteus maximus functional segments

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Selkowitz DM, Beneck GJ, Powers CM (2016) J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 46(9):794-799

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: For the cranial segment, transducer angled 45 degrees toward the sacrum on the posterior surface of the hip joint, in the upper quadrant of the gluteal region, roughly 8 cm lateral to the sacrum. Scanning then continues distally along the posterior thigh for the middle and caudal segments.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Most superficial of three muscle masses lying over the iliac cortex; gluteus minimus is deepest and gluteus medius lies between.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Three injection points are indicated, one per segment, because the arborization mapping found a separate zone in each: 40-70% on line a (cranial), 30-60% on line b (middle), 40-70% on line c (caudal). NO motor_endplate_zones entry is recorded for this muscle, because the definitions of lines a, b and c sit in a list that full-text extraction dropped -- a percentage without both ends of its reference line is not an injection target, and the endpoints are not inferred. Consult the original figure before using these numbers. The three-segment scheme also does not match this atlas's superior/inferior split. Injected where spasticity limits hip flexion and impairs swing limb advancement; reported also to improve ulcerative lesions in the gluteal and intergluteal regions, and to relieve pain in localized contracture after total hip arthroplasty.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part III -- Proximal Lower Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(5):240 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17050240 -- review synthesis of the intramuscular neural arborization literature it cites

trigger_points.location_description: Upper-medial fibers close to the sacral origin
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Pain over the sacroiliac joint and medially in the buttock along the gluteal cleft and gluteal fold, occasionally spreading onto the posterior thigh
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in triggerpoints.net, 'Gluteus Maximus' (http://www.triggerpoints.net/muscle/gluteus-maximus); topography corroborated by real cadaveric anatomy: Akamatsu FE, Yendo TM, Rhode C, Itezerote AM, Hojaij F, Andrade M, Hsing WT, Jacomo AL (2017) 'Anatomical Basis of the Myofascial Trigger Points of the Gluteus Maximus Muscle.' Biomed Res Int 2017:4821968, doi:10.1155/2017/4821968 (https://doi.org/10.1155/2017/4821968) -- retrieved via PubMed, found the clinically described trigger-point topography matches inferior gluteal nerve branch entry points into the muscle

trigger_points.location_description: Mid-belly, immediately above the ischial tuberosity (the most commonly active site); a third, less common site lies in the medial/inferior fibers near the coccyx
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: From the mid-belly site: diffuse aching over the entire buttock and lower sacrum, worse sitting or climbing stairs. From the medial/inferior fibers: pain concentrated over the coccyx, which can mimic coccydynia
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Prolonged sitting on a hard surface or thick wallet, hip flexion contracture, sacroiliac joint dysfunction, and intramuscular gluteal injections
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual (Travell JG, Simons DG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 2: The Lower Extremities, 1st ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1992; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019) -- as cited in triggerpoints.net, 'Gluteus Maximus' (http://www.triggerpoints.net/muscle/gluteus-maximus); topography corroborated by real cadaveric anatomy: Akamatsu FE, Yendo TM, Rhode C, Itezerote AM, Hojaij F, Andrade M, Hsing WT, Jacomo AL (2017) 'Anatomical Basis of the Myofascial Trigger Points of the Gluteus Maximus Muscle.'
